The problem starts with the second drone (and all subsequent ones) due to a sync failure between the Host and Clients: When the Host is the operator (2nd drone): The drone only deals damage if the victim is a Client player. If the Host tries to damage anything else (like bots), no damage is dealt. Even when the damage to a player registers, there is no visual explosion effect for the victim — the drone just disappears. When a Client is the operator (2nd drone): The drone deals no damage at all (neither to players nor bots). The person controlling the drone hears the explosion sound, but for everyone else, the drone simply vanishes upon detonation without any effect. General behavior: For anyone who is not currently controlling the drone, the 2nd drone simply vanishes without an explosion or damage at the moment of activation. It seems the damage registration and visual effects ‘break’ for every drone instance after the first one, with a strange exception for Host-to-Client player damage. It’s possible that this is related to the recent synchronization update in Fika.

comments.author: pein
comments.body_html:
Thanks for taking the time to test the mod and for writing up your feedback. I’m glad to hear you weren’t able to reproduce the issue with bringing the drone equipment into raids.

As for the suicide drone controls, they’re intentionally much more difficult than the recon drone, and that’s by design rather than something I overlooked. The recon drone is meant to be a utility tool. You’re expected to fly it around carefully, gather information, and generally spend a fair amount of time in the air. The suicide drone serves a completely different role. It’s a disposable weapon that can instantly kill or heavily damage a target if used correctly, so I don’t think it should be as forgiving to control.

Making it fly like the recon drone or adding a forward boost would dramatically lower the skill floor and make successful hits much more consistent. At that point, it starts becoming less about learning to pilot it and more about simply steering it into whatever you want to delete. I think that would make it far too reliable, especially against AI, and it would remove a lot of the tension and satisfaction that comes from actually mastering it.

One of my goals with this mod is to avoid solving every inconvenience with a configuration option. While I don’t mind adding settings when they make sense, I also don’t want to end up with dozens of toggles that fundamentally change the intended gameplay. If I don’t personally think a mechanic improves the experience, I’d rather leave it as-is than add an option that effectively bypasses the design.

I completely understand why you’d prefer the recon drone’s handling—it would definitely feel more comfortable and easier to use. But the discomfort is intentional. The suicide drone is supposed to feel harder to control, more stressful to pilot, and more punishing if you make a mistake. That’s part of what differentiates it from the recon drone beyond simply replacing the camera with an explosive.

So while I appreciate the suggestion, I don’t plan on adding either a recon-style handling toggle or a Shift boost. I’d rather keep the distinction between the two drones meaningful than make them feel like the same platform with different payloads.

That said, I still appreciate you taking the time to give feedback. Even if I don’t implement every suggestion, hearing what people struggle with helps me understand how the mod is being used in practice.

tldr: no
